title: Sam Smith, Stella Lefty, Weezer & More: New Music Friday Guide
summary: Check out the must-hear releases of the week.
body: Billboard’s Friday Music Guide serves as a handy guide to New Music Friday’s most essential releases each week — the key music that everyone will be talking about today, and that will be dominating playlists this weekend and beyond. Last week , we featured Phoebe Bridgers, Katseye, Ayra Starr, Troye Sivan and more. This week, Sam Smith shares their new album, Hazel Eyes ; Stella Lefty releases her highly-anticipated debut set; and Weezer drops its 20th (!) full-length… plus much more. Check out all of this week’s picks below: Sam Smith, Hazel Eyes On “Constant Companion” — one of 12 tracks on Smith’s fifth album — the English singer-songwriter chooses to spotlight their impressive range, singing in their deeper, lower register to start and slowly softening into a more familiar tone that allows their voice to soar. Accompanied by gentle percussion and choral harmonies throughout, delicate keys and an acoustic guitar kick in later and help carry the song. But it’s in the last minute, after the addition of winding strings, that it reaches its peak as Smith bellows with renewed intention: “’cause you, you are my constant companion.&#8221…

title: Garth Brooks’ ‘Blame It All On My Roots’ Tour: Every Song Played On Opening Night
summary: The country superstar returned to the road with a show taken right out of 1997.
body: Garth Brooks opened his Blame It All On My Roots tour in Indianapolis’s Gainbridge Fieldhouse on Thursday (Aug. 20) night, taking fans back to his ‘90s heyday. Announced in July, the trek is a recreation of Brooks’ 1996-1998 massive world tour, down to the set design, lighting rig and famous spinning drum pod. On opening night, he even kept to a retro setlist, playing no songs that came out after 1997. Brooks took the stage slightly before 8 p.m. A grand piano came up through the floor with pianist Dave Gant playing the opening strains of, appropriately enough, “The Old Stuff,” as Brooks then rose up through the grand piano, singing the first lines from the 1995’s Fresh Horses cut: “Whoa, I said a little prayer tonight/’fore I came on stage/as I came walking past the drivers and the locals on the union wage.” In addition to Gant, Brooks’ band includes many players who have been playing with him since at least the ‘90s, including drummer Mike Palmer, fiddle player Jimmy Mattingly, pedal steel guitarist Bruce Bouton bassist Mark Greenwood. title: ENHYPEN Drops Latest Installment in ‘THE SIN’  Series With ‘BLISS’: Stream It Now
summary: THE SIN : BLISS is the K-pop group's eighth mini-album.
body: Bliss out, ENHYPEN is back with six fresh tunes. At the stroke of midnight, the K-pop heavyweights dropped THE SIN : BLISS , the group’s eighth mini album and the second installment in the ongoing THE SIN series. THE SIN : BLISS is ENHYPEN’s first release since HEESEUNG announced  that he would go his own way and pursue a solo career. Now a six-piece of Jake, Jay, Sunghoon, Sunoo, Jungwon and Ni-ki, the band recently completed the Latin American and United States legs of their BLOOD SAGA trek, their largest world tour to date . ENHYPEN’s busy year has taken the group to Brazil, where they performed on late-night television program The Noite com Danilo Gentili ; and Mexico City for a 2026 FIFA World Cup celebration event at Campo Marte. Along the way, the group took part in San Diego Comic-Con 2026, where they introduced global audiences to “DARK MOON,” HYBE’s original story inspired by ENHYPEN’s narrative universe. title: Stella Lefty’s ‘Long Way Home’: All 14 Tracks Ranked
summary: The "Boston" singer-songwriter releases her first full-length set, full of winsome, appealing tunes.
body: Stella Lefty emerged seemingly out of nowhere this year with the track “Boston,” a toe-tapping, romantic country-pop smash that interpolates Noah Kahan ’s “Stick Season.” The tune, one of the summer’s biggest hits , reached No. 3 on both Billboard’s Hot 100 and Country Songs charts following “Thinking ‘Bout You,” her only other previous charting song, which peaked at 50 on Country Songs. Bolstered by the success of “Boston,” Lefty’s EP, Is This Heaven, debuted at No. 9 on the Top Country Albums in late May, making her the first woman to land in the top 10 with her initial release this year. All six songs from that effort are on Long Way Home, her first full-length album out Friday (Aug. 21) via Atlantic Outpost. The album, helmed by British producer Joe Reeves (Lil Durk, Morgan Wallen , Jelly Roll), is extremely likeable. Reeves’ low-key production perfectly complements Lefty’s sweet, unadorned vocals, creating what feels like an uncomplicated, authentic effort and a solid introduction to a formidable, developing talent. Her voice is wrapped around primarily acoustic instrumentation, especially banjo and mandolin, that adds to the album’s overall pleasing blend of coun…

title: Sam Smith’s ‘Hazel Eyes’: All 12 Songs Ranked
summary: The British singer-songwriter's fifth album is deeply personal, revealing a more assured side of the star while offering an intimate glimpse into the people and places closest to them.
body: With Hazel Eyes , Sam Smith charts a fresh, emboldened emotional hinterland. Across the London-born singer’s four previous albums, the question of who exists beyond that distinct, aching, soulful voice has loomed large. Smith initially built a career, after all, on the strange alchemy of writing about heartbreak from largely hypothetical pain; they penned 2014 global smash In the Lonely Hour before ever experiencing a breakup. The albums that followed gradually filled in the blanks – desire, growth, personal identity, sex – though with the sense of an artist discovering themselves and testing out what they want to say to the world. In the process, they have scooped billions of streams, five Grammy Awards and seven Billboard Hot 100 top 10 hits — and with 2023 Kim Petras collab “Unholy,” became the first openly nonbinary artist to top the chart. At times, Smith’s fifth full-length effort gets closer than ever to answering that question. The dual muses across Hazel Eyes become figures in a wider romantic mythology; even when their partner, the (hazel-eyed) fashion designer Christian Cowan, or their newly adopted home of New York City enters the frame,…

title: How Gang of Youths Took a ‘Whole Different Approach’ With New Era
summary: The Australian alternative rock group this week shared "Things Take Time," their first new music in four years.
body: Gang of Youths are back. This is not a drill. The chart-topping, multiple ARIA Award winners have emerged from hibernation with “Things Take Time” (via Mosy Recordings / Sony Music Australia / RCA U.K. and Arista U.S.), the alternative rock act’s first new music in four years. Written by bandmates David Le’aupepe, Tom Hobden, Donnie Borzestowski and Jung Kim, “Things Take Time,” with its orchestral flourishes, is a mature, more mellow version of a band that cut its teeth in Sydney’s pub scene, and, by 2017 , had moved into position as one of Australia’s preeminent rock bands. “Things Take Time” is a meditation on patience, and the swings and roundabouts that are the playground of life. Of growth, decay, and regrowth. “It’s in it’s namesake, but it took a f—ing long time to make a three-minute song,” Kim tells Billboard with a laugh. “It took three years to make a three-minute song.” Then, “lightning struck” and the thunder followed as Le’aupepe reached into his bag of tricks, chords came, and the song flowed. title: EBiDAN’s ‘Yes! Tokyo’ Tops Japan Hot 100 as Florence Road Makes Chart Debut Following First Japan Visit at Summer Sonic
body: EBiDAN’s “Yes! Tokyo” hits No. 1 on the Billboard Japan Hot 100 , on the chart released Aug. 19. Released Aug. 11 to mark the group’s 15th anniversary, the commemorative track launched with exceptional physical sales of 1,313,739 copies to rule the metric, while also landing at No. 3 on streaming for a commanding overall point total. Several member-group “ taiken nyugaku ” (experience enrollment) versions of the track also charted simultaneously — the M!LK version debuts at No. 18, the GNJB version at No. 46, the Bullet Train version at No. 66, and the ONE N’ ONLY version at No. 80 — bringing the total to five versions of the same song inside the top 100 in a single week. Hearts2Hearts’ “ICONIC HEART” debuts at No. 2. The SM Entertainment girl group’s Japan debut single was released Aug. 12 and sold 65,176 copies to hit No. 2 for sales while ruling radio airplay, marking a strong showing for a debut release. title: Gracie Abrams Says ‘Hit the Wall’ Became the ‘North Star’ for Her ‘Daughter From Hell’ Album & Yet ‘I Don’t Remember Writing It’
summary: "I just remember it being done," the singer/songwriter recalls of the lead single.
body: Gracie Abrams didn’t exactly know what Daughter From Hell was going to become when she wrote “Hit the Wall.” As it turned out, the song would actually help her figure it out, and ultimately introduced the album that would earn her first No. 1 on the Billboard 200 . During a recent appearance on Jake Shane’s Therapuss podcast, Abrams vulnerably talked about the circumstances surrounding the creation of “Hit the Wall,” revealing that the song became the “north star” of her third studio album.
